subject: humanities
passage: The bagpipe is the national instrument of Scotland. It is played at Scottish weddings, parades, and military ceremonies, and a lone piper on a hillside is one of the most familiar images of the country. Many people therefore assume that the instrument was invented there.
passage_b: Instruments made of a bag and a set of pipes were played in many parts of the world long before Scotland became known for them. Roman writers mention a bagpipe, and medieval paintings show pipers across Europe. Today bagpipes are still part of folk music in Spain, Italy, Bulgaria, and parts of the Middle East. The Scottish Highland pipe is one member of a large family.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption in Text 1?

choices.A: By claiming that bagpipes are no longer played anywhere except Scotland
choices.B: By agreeing that the instrument was first invented in Scotland
choices.C: By pointing out that bagpipes have long been played in many places outside Scotland
choices.D: By arguing that Scottish bagpipes sound better than those of other countries

explanation.why: Text 1 says people assume the bagpipe "was invented" in Scotland. Text 2 replies that bagpipes were played "in many parts of the world long before Scotland became known for them" and are still played in Spain, Italy, Bulgaria, and the Middle East. The author of Text 2 would answer the assumption by pointing to this wider history.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says the opposite: bagpipes are "still part of folk music" in several other countries.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says bagpipes existed elsewhere long before Scotland became known for them, so its author would not agree.
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 gives examples of bagpipes in ancient Rome, medieval Europe, and modern folk music in several countries.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 never compares how the instruments sound.
